channel.title: The Box Plus Network - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Box Plus Network (boxplus.com)

item.title: Starmer survives botched coup as Burnham backs him
item.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer has issued a defiant challenge to any rivals for his job that he will "never walk away" from his mandate to govern.

item.title: Starmer received a ‘roar of support’ from his cabinet, says Labour Party chair
item.description: We were joined by the chair of the Labour Party Anna Turley.

item.title: Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says he backs Starmer
item.description: New research by the Resolution Foundation has confirmed the financial pressures facing those on lower incomes.

item.title: What to make of Labour’s ‘disaster’ this week – MPs debate
item.description: We were joined by Labour MP Andy McDonald and Conservative MP Harriet Cross.

item.title: Boys stabbed at London school – counter-terror police investigating
item.description: Police say they have arrested a boy who's believed to be 13 on suspicion of attempted murder after two other boys, aged 12 and 13, were stabbed at a school in Brent.

item.title: Congressman names six high profile men included in the Epstein files
item.description: The ripples of the Epstein scandal continue to grow in the United States, where a Democratic congressman has named six high profile men who are allegedly included in the Epstein files.

item.title: Nuneaton: Asylum seeker guilty of raping 12-year-old girl
item.description: An asylum seeker has been found guilty of abducting and raping a 12-year-old girl in Nuneaton, in an attack which sparked protests in July last year.

item.title: The key Atlantic current that could change Europe’s climate forever
item.description: Western Europe could face winters as cold as Canada because of the impact of climate change on a key Atlantic current, known as the AMOC, which helps regulate our weather.

item.title: Call for action on kids targeted with weight loss and skin lightening ads online
item.description: The Children's Commissioner is calling for urgent action to tackle online ads targeting children on social media which promote potentially harmful appearance changing products.

item.title: ‘Massive fines on tech companies’ could stop online ads targeting kids, says children’s commissioner
item.description: We asked Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England what the government could be doing to put pressure on tech companies so they start responding to potentially harmful ads targeting kids online.
